changelog: Replace C2 severity to make NP completeness part of what makes a left-span fragment worse or milder — addresses the primary finding that the scorer currently prefers earlier fragmenting cuts inside NPs while the target prefers the later cut that preserves the full NP.
findings: When two cuts fall inside the same nominal expression, the prompt prefers earlier fragmenting cuts while the target prefers the later cut that preserves the full NP.
The prompt cuts where the left span is a subject/NP but the predicate (finite verb or auxiliary) immediately follows, producing a fragment that the continuation overturns or completes.

edits.was: - If the left-side stretch is read alone, is it a coherent, self-contained propo
edits.now: - If the left-side stretch is read alone, is it a coherent, self-contained propo

diagnosis.why: The edit made NP-completeness part of the left-fragment severity, so the scorer reduced many cuts that split NPs (giving a small net gain). However, that change often achieved NP preservation by moving the preferred cut earlier (detaching tiny left fragments or cutting before an NP) which harmed a sizable set of mid-length examples; improvements are concentrated in the very short latency bins (≤3, ≤5) while ≤7/≤10 bins show small losses. Rank_depth falls at depth1 and rises at depth2, indicating the edit shifted the top choice rather than uniformly improving deeper rankings.
diagnosis.lesson: When increasing NP-completeness weight, preserve or improve top-1 alignment—avoid causing the model to favor earlier boundary placements that detach tiny left fragments even if they avoid cutting inside NPs.
